direction.name: Breezeway Courtyard Villa
direction.concept: A contemporary Caribbean composition organized as a strong, low limestone plinth facing the arrival court, with a lighter, offset upper bedroom bar and a deeply shaded south-facing garden veranda. The asymmetrical entry pavilion and stepped upper volume give the villa a distinct identity from every approach while preserving a broad, calm pool garden.
hierarchy: Primary mass: broad two-storey central living volume
Secondary mass: lower east bedroom/service wing
Arrival marker: compact west entry pavilion projecting toward the north forecourt
Garden threshold: full-width covered south veranda
Crowning mass: offset upper bedroom bar with a smaller east suite volume
direction.roofLanguage: Low, crisply edged Caribbean roof planes with deep overhangs; the upper volumes should read as floating shade canopies above recessed glazing and shaded terraces.
direction.entrance: Arrival is from the north into a generous forecourt. The projecting west entry pavilion creates a protected, memorable approach before guests turn into a tall, shaded entry recess beneath the offset upper mass.
direction.outdoorLiving: The south side is the dedicated garden face: a 4.5 m-deep covered veranda extends from the main living mass and forms the shaded transition to the future pool terrace and approximately 9 m-deep swimming pool beyond.
direction.landscape: Maintain an open north arrival lawn and forecourt, with palms framing the entry pavilion. The south garden is a broad resort-like lawn and palm grove around the pool, with layered tropical planting concentrated along the east and west boundaries.

blocks.role: primary ground-floor living, dining, kitchen and bedroom mass
secondary ground-floor bedroom and support wing
projecting arrival entry and stair pavilion

design.statement: Offline construction and visual rehearsal on the unchanged real Terra house: an axial pool garden, shaded veranda dining, warm limestone promenades and composed tropical boundaries.
intentions: Connect the shaded veranda to the pool with a continuous dry walking surface.
Use measured paired palms and layered boundary planting rather than random scattering.
